title: Ledger in the document: load, verify, replay, serialize
goal: The document boots from its own <script type="application/document-ledger">, verifies the chain, replays to state, and serializes itself to a clean HTML string (engine + updated ledger, no rendered DOM).
scope: Boot: read the ledger before rendering; parse, verify, replay; integrity failure → banner + read-only; unknown fmt/op → read-only + message
Pristine template capture at boot (documentElement.outerHTML before any rendering, ledger replaced by a placeholder); serialize = "<!doctype html>" + template with the new ledger
window.webdoc v0: version, state(), hash(), ledger(), selection() (stub until E1-007), toHTML(); documented in SPEC.md
Browser append path: event → canonical line → in-memory ledger text, heads update

rules.rule: A typed "</script>" or "<!--" never breaks the file.
Engine script bytes in a saved file equal dist (CSP hash stays valid).

metrics: load of the 10k-word fixture ≤ 300 ms desktop / ≤ 1 s mobile

criteria: Fixtures (empty, EN 10k words, DE, stress with </script>, <!--, U+2028, ZWJ emoji, CJK, RTL) load on all 5 targets; webdoc.hash() equals the Node reference hash.
serialize → load in a fresh page gives an equal hash; a second serialize is byte-identical, on all targets.
The saved HTML has exactly one ledger script and one engine script; the browser executes it without CSP violation.
Tampered fixtures (byte flip, deleted line, swapped lines) show the integrity banner, are read-only and log no exception.
An unknown-op fixture opens read-only with a message.
Load + verify + replay of the 10k-word fixture ≤ 300 ms on each desktop target and ≤ 1 s on each mobile target (values recorded).
acceptance.critic: Criteria-based on all 5 targets; the gap is the first unproven criterion.
